answer: An agent economy can charge each new identity a small refundable bond before it trades. One person who spins up a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds, so the attack costs real money up front while honest agents pay once and get the bond back for good behavior. A violet badge could mark accounts that passed a slow reputation check, and a prism of independent verifiers could confirm each badge from different angles. Once an agent reaches the zenith of its trust score, its trades settle faster, so fakes stay at the bottom where they earn nothing.
